audit_scope.audit_only_rule: This artifact freezes benchmark-target caveats for mechanism_fingerprint_v1_8fp and does not relabel any row.

freeze_decision_summary.primary_metric_rule: Use mechanism_fingerprint_id as the primary target only for seed_fingerprint labels whose fingerprint audit status is coherent_v1 or coarse_but_acceptable_v1.
freeze_decision_summary.caveat: Several kept fingerprints are intentionally coarse chemistry buckets; the audit preserves their caveats and future split candidates instead of editing v1 labels.

fingerprints_excluded_or_flagged_for_sec.reason: singleton_underpowered at one M-CSA member; keep as an OOD/tail diagnostic until additional radical SAM labels exist.
three-member bucket mixes true adenosylcobalamin radical mutases with an adenosyltransferase-like cobalamin row; use secondary-only until split or re-review.
two-member oxygen-transfer tail; likely underrepresented relative to real enzyme-space coverage.

unresolved_ontology_questions: Should metal_dependent_hydrolase be split into metalloprotease, nuclease/phosphoesterase, deaminase/amidohydrolase, carbonic-anhydrase/hydration, and NTPase/phosphohydrolase children before a v2 target?
Should plp_dependent_enzyme split transamination, decarboxylation, racemization, beta/gamma elimination, glycogen-phosphorylase-like acid catalysis, and coupled PLP-radical cases before a v2 target?

Should flavin_dehydrogenase_reductase move oxygenase-like rows to flavin_monooxygenase and split hydride-transfer reductases, oxidases/dehydrogenases, electron-transfer proteins, and photolyase-like photochemistry?
Should heme_peroxidase_oxidase split P450 monooxygenase, peroxidase/catalase, terminal oxidase, nitric-oxide/nitrite reductase, and heme oxygenase families?
Should cobalamin_radical_rearrangement exclude cobalamin adenosyltransferase rows from radical rearrangement metrics or receive a separate cobalamin-adenosylation fingerprint?
downstream_benchmark_rules: Primary target remains mechanism_fingerprint_id only for seed_fingerprint labels whose fingerprint audit status is coherent_v1 or coarse_but_acceptable_v1.
out_of_scope / none_of_above is the abstention secondary target and must be stratified by hard-negative tier when possible.

Hard negatives are not one bucket: easy = non-enzymes/non-catalytic where present; medium = known enzymes outside the 8 fingerprints; hard = enzymes sharing fold/cofactor/active-site geometry but different chemistry.
Bootstrap comparisons must resample sequence or structure clusters, not individual entries, when the split is cluster-derived.
EC/family prior is a leakage-aware reference only; report the gap between EC prior and learned models, do not use EC/name/prose as production predictive features.

External AFDB/Swiss-Prot pilot should primarily test OOD abstention behavior and embedding-space structure unless curated ground-truth mechanism labels exist; do not pretend propagated labels are independent truth.
Within-fingerprint diversity check plan: report whether correct predictions span diverse sequence/structure neighborhoods or only interpolate inside tight clusters.

Win condition is conjunctive: a representation model must improve mechanism prediction against baselines AND maintain or improve calibrated abstention on tail/hard-negative cases. Macro-F1 gain alone is not a win.

same_fingerprint_pairs_that_look_mechani.concern: Metallo-beta-lactamase amide hydrolysis and Mg-linked GTP hydrolysis share metal/water logic but differ in substrate class and reaction-center geometry.
Zinc metalloprotease peptide hydrolysis and zinc-supported hydrolytic deamination are both water-activation mechanisms but likely separate v2 subfamilies.
Classic aminotransferase chemistry and glycogen-phosphorylase-like PLP acid catalysis share PLP but not the same bond-change class.
Disulfide reductase hydride transfer and photolyase photochemical electron transfer are both flavin redox but not the same reaction-center operation.
Terminal heme-copper oxygen reduction and P450 substrate monooxygenation share heme redox chemistry but are distinct catalytic operations.
Adenosylcobalamin mutase radical rearrangement and cobalamin adenosyltransferase-like chemistry should not be treated as equivalent target labels.

different_fingerprint_pairs_that_may_be_.concern: Aromatic flavin hydroxylase and a phenol monooxygenase-like row may belong to the same flavin oxygen-transfer v2 family if peroxide/oxygen insertion is confirmed.
FMN/FAD oxygenation rows may be split inconsistently between oxygen-transfer and broad flavin-redox targets.
PLP plus SAM/Fe-S aminomutase chemistry and radical SAM chemistry share radical cofactor logic; a coupled PLP-radical v2 family may be cleaner than either parent alone.
Multi-cofactor flavin/heme electron-transfer rows may be assigned by the dominant cofactor rather than a single reaction-center target.

fingerprints.shared_catalytic_operation: Yes: representative members share nucleophilic acyl substitution through a serine acyl-enzyme intermediate followed by water deacylation or closely related perhydrolysis.
fingerprints.shared_residue_role_pattern: Strong: catalytic Ser nucleophile plus His general base plus Asp/Glu acid/orienter is the repeated role pattern; rare Ser-His-His or perhydrolase variants are caveats, not broad counterexamples.
fingerprints.shared_cofactor_or_metal_logic: Strong: no obligate metal or organic cofactor is part of the target logic; metal-dependent rows are excluded unless the Ser-His-acid triad is the central mechanism.
fingerprints.shared_reaction_center_logic: Strong: acyl heteroatom bond hydrolysis/perhydrolysis around an acyl-enzyme reaction center is consistent across protease, esterase, lipase, cutinase, and polyesterase representatives.

entries_that_may_not_belong.reason: Cofactor-free chloride peroxidase/perhydrolase chemistry is acyl-enzyme Ser-His-Asp-like but may deserve a perhydrolase child target.
Ser-His-His assemblin variant lacks the canonical Asp/Glu acid slot and should stay a v1 caveat.

fingerprints.model_benchmark_implication: Eligible for primary mechanism_fingerprint_id metrics; require within-fingerprint diversity checks so a model is not only interpolating among tight serine-protease or lipase neighborhoods.

fingerprints.shared_catalytic_operation: Mostly yes at v1 granularity: representatives share metal-assisted water/hydroxide activation for bond cleavage or hydrolytic group removal, but the target intentionally collapses several metal-water submechanisms.
fingerprints.shared_residue_role_pattern: Moderate: His/Asp/Glu/Cys metal ligands and acid/base water activators recur, but leaving-group stabilizers and substrate-binding residues are family-specific.
fingerprints.shared_cofactor_or_metal_logic: Strong but coarse: Zn, Mg, Mn, Fe, Ni, Co, or surrogate divalent metal centers are central to the catalytic water logic; metal identity is not yet a separate target axis.
fingerprints.shared_reaction_center_logic: Moderate: all kept rows involve metal-activated hydrolytic chemistry, but peptide, beta-lactam, phosphate, nucleotide, deamination, carbonic-anhydrase, and NTPase reaction centers are not interchangeable.

entries_that_may_not_belong.reason: Protein-synthesizing GTPase is phosphate hydrolysis with metal/NTP context and should be a hard tail caveat, not evidence that all NTPases are metal hydrolases.
Carbonate dehydratase/carbonic anhydrase uses zinc-bound hydroxide chemistry but does not fit the same scissile-bond logic as proteases or nucleases.

fingerprints.model_benchmark_implication: Eligible for primary metrics as a coarse class only; report per-subfamily diversity and do not treat wins driven by zinc metalloprotease or nuclease interpolation as general metal-hydrolase understanding.

fingerprints.shared_catalytic_operation: Yes at PLP-cofactor granularity: representatives use PLP Schiff-base/electron-sink chemistry or PLP-assisted acid/base chemistry to stabilize carbanion-like intermediates.
fingerprints.shared_residue_role_pattern: Moderate to strong: Lys-PLP internal aldimine and nearby acid/base or phosphate-binding residues recur, but individual acid/base identities and substrate-control residues vary widely.
fingerprints.shared_cofactor_or_metal_logic: Strong: PLP/LLP/PMP/P5P context is central; coupled SAM/Fe-S rows are caveats rather than the dominant v1 logic.
fingerprints.shared_reaction_center_logic: Moderate: C-N, C-C, C-S, beta/gamma elimination, racemization, decarboxylation, transamination, and phosphorylase-like reactions all use PLP but do not share one substrate bond class.

entries_that_may_not_belong.reason: Glycogen phosphorylase uses PLP in a phosphate/acid-catalysis role rather than the canonical amino-acid external-aldimine target logic.
Lysine 2,3-aminomutase requires PLP plus SAM/Fe-S radical chemistry and may be cleaner as a coupled PLP-radical child.

fingerprints.model_benchmark_implication: Eligible for primary metrics as a PLP-cofactor mechanism target; require diversity checks across transaminase, decarboxylase, lyase, racemase, and coupled-radical neighborhoods.

fingerprints.shared_catalytic_operation: Not evaluable from the registry: the sole member is NikJ with [4Fe-4S]-AdoMet radical chemistry.
fingerprints.shared_residue_role_pattern: Underpowered: Cys cluster-ligand and SAM-binding motif logic is plausible but cannot be audited across representative M-CSA diversity with one member.
fingerprints.shared_cofactor_or_metal_logic: Underpowered but specific: [4Fe-4S] plus S-adenosylmethionine is the intended logic.
fingerprints.shared_reaction_center_logic: Underpowered: radical C-H activation/rearrangement cannot be distinguished from broader radical chemistry with one label.
fingerprints.singleton_or_underpowered_reason: Likely underrepresented due to M-CSA/atlas coverage and the current conservative import gate; radical SAM enzyme-space is broad but only one seed_fingerprint label is present.
fingerprints.model_benchmark_implication: Use only as a tail/OOD diagnostic and do not include in primary supervised fingerprint metrics until more independently curated radical SAM positives exist.

fingerprints.shared_catalytic_operation: Mixed: m_csa:62 and m_csa:63 are coherent adenosylcobalamin radical rearrangements, while m_csa:853 appears closer to cobalamin adenosylation/adenosyltransferase chemistry.
fingerprints.shared_residue_role_pattern: Weak: cobalamin-binding and substrate-orienting residues are not enough to make all three rows a shared radical rearrangement residue-role target.
fingerprints.shared_cofactor_or_metal_logic: Partial: adenosylcobalamin/cobalamin context is shared, but cofactor presence alone collapses rearrangement and cofactor-biosynthesis/adenosylation logic.
fingerprints.shared_reaction_center_logic: Weak: carbon-skeleton rearrangement and ammonia-elimination-like radical chemistry do not cover cobalamin adenosyltransferase-like reaction centers.

entries_that_may_not_belong.reason: Cobalamin ligand/cofactor context is strong, but the named adenosyltransferase-like chemistry is not a radical rearrangement benchmark target.

fingerprints.model_benchmark_implication: Keep labels frozen for provenance, but exclude this fingerprint from the primary metric; report it as secondary tail evidence until m_csa:853 is re-reviewed or a separate cobalamin-adenosylation target exists.

fingerprints.shared_catalytic_operation: Plausible but underpowered: both rows use flavin oxygen-transfer chemistry, one aromatic hydroxylase and one alkanal monooxygenase.
fingerprints.shared_residue_role_pattern: Underpowered: flavin-binding and NAD(P)H/substrate-orienting motifs are plausible, but two rows cannot establish a robust residue-role pattern.
fingerprints.shared_cofactor_or_metal_logic: Plausible: FAD/FMN plus NAD(P)H oxygen activation is the intended shared logic.
fingerprints.shared_reaction_center_logic: Plausible but sparse: oxygen insertion/hydroxylation is shared, but substrate classes differ and the current registry may have oxygenase-like rows in flavin_dehydrogenase_reductase.
fingerprints.singleton_or_underpowered_reason: Likely underrepresented by current M-CSA/atlas coverage and prior conservative imports; real flavin oxygenase space is larger than two labels.
fingerprints.model_benchmark_implication: Use as secondary tail/OOD analysis only; do not reward or penalize primary representation models on a two-member oxygen-transfer class.

fingerprints.shared_catalytic_operation: Mostly yes at v1 granularity: representatives share flavin-mediated hydride/electron transfer, but oxidase, reductase, electron-transfer, and photochemical subfamilies are collapsed.
fingerprints.shared_residue_role_pattern: Moderate: flavin-binding motifs and redox acid/base or electron-transfer residues recur, but specific catalytic residues differ substantially by family.
fingerprints.shared_cofactor_or_metal_logic: Strong: FAD/FMN is central. Multi-cofactor rows with heme or Fe-S are acceptable only when flavin is the principal redox relay.
fingerprints.shared_reaction_center_logic: Moderate: hydride/electron transfer without committed oxygen insertion is the intended rule, but several oxygenase-like names need future adjudication.

entries_that_may_not_belong.reason: Phenol 2-monooxygenase name suggests oxygen-transfer chemistry that may belong with flavin_monooxygenase if local peroxide/oxygen insertion evidence confirms it.
DszC-like flavin oxygenation/sulfur oxidation may be closer to flavin_monooxygenase than to non-oxygen-insertion redox transfer.
Mandelonitrile lyase naming and chemistry should be rechecked against flavin redox being the true catalytic target rather than binding/context evidence.

fingerprints.model_benchmark_implication: Eligible for primary metrics only as a broad flavin-redox target; evaluate oxygenase-like and photolyase-like rows as caveat strata and report confusion against flavin_monooxygenase.

fingerprints.shared_catalytic_operation: Yes at broad heme-redox granularity: all representative rows depend on heme-centered redox chemistry, but peroxide, oxygen-reduction, monooxygenation, nitrite/NO reduction, and heme oxygenase operations are distinct.
fingerprints.shared_residue_role_pattern: Moderate: His/Cys/Tyr heme ligation and nearby acid/base or electron-transfer residues recur, but P450, peroxidase, catalase, oxidase, and reductase families use different role patterns.
fingerprints.shared_cofactor_or_metal_logic: Strong: heme or heme-copper redox logic is central; H2O2/O2/NO/nitrite substrate logic differs by subfamily.
fingerprints.shared_reaction_center_logic: Coarse: heme-mediated redox is shared, but oxygen insertion, peroxide dismutation/reduction, terminal O2 reduction, and nitrogen-oxide reduction should be split in v2.

entries_that_may_not_belong.reason: Ubiquinol-cytochrome-c reductase may be more electron-transfer-chain context than a single local heme oxidase/peroxidase target.
Hydroperoxide dehydratase chemistry may require a family-specific split rather than broad heme redox.

fingerprints.model_benchmark_implication: Eligible for primary metrics as broad heme-redox only; require subfamily-stratified reporting so P450/peroxidase/oxidase/catalase interpolation is visible.
